pharm: Semisynthetic lipopeptide echinocandin that inhibits synthesis of beta-(1,3)-D-glucan, an integral component of the fungal cell wall
quick: 70 mg IV loading dose Day 1, then 50 mg once daily (no load for esophageal candidiasis)
May cause fetal harm (animal data); advise of potential risk
Unknown if present in human milk; weigh benefits and risks
Moderate impairment (Child-Pugh 7-9): reduce to 35 mg daily
Liver function tests; signs of hypersensitivity
summary: Caspofungin acetate is an intravenous echinocandin antifungal indicated in adults and children 3 months and older for empirical therapy of presumed fungal infection in febrile neutropenic patients, candidemia and certain Candida infections, esophageal candidiasis, and invasive aspergillosis refractory to or intolerant of other therapy. The usual adult regimen is a 70 mg loading dose then 50 mg daily, reduced to 35 mg daily in moderate hepatic impairment.
indications: Empirical therapy for presumed fungal infections in febrile, neutropenic patients
Candidemia and other Candida infections: intra-abdominal abscesses, peritonitis, and pleural space infections
Invasive aspergillosis in patients refractory to or intolerant of other therapies

dosage.r: Most indications (empirical therapy, candidemia/Candida infections, invasive aspergillosis)
dosage.d: 70 mg IV loading dose on Day 1, then 50 mg once daily
dosage.n: Infuse slowly over approximately 1 hour; do not give as IV bolus

dosage.d: Reduce to 35 mg once daily (with a 70 mg load on Day 1 where appropriate)
dosage.n: No data in severe hepatic impairment
Consider 70 mg daily also with nevirapine, efavirenz, carbamazepine, dexamethasone, or phenytoin

dosage.r: All approved indications (dose by body surface area)
dosage.d: 70 mg/m2 loading dose Day 1, then 50 mg/m2 once daily
dosage.n: Loading and daily doses must not exceed 70 mg regardless of calculated dose

admin: Administer by slow IV infusion over approximately 1 hour
Do not administer by IV bolus
Do not mix or co-infuse with other medications
Do not use diluents containing dextrose (alpha-D-glucose)
Reconstitute lyophilized powder per labeling; discard unused portion
moa: Caspofungin is a semisynthetic echinocandin antifungal that non-competitively inhibits the synthesis of beta-(1,3)-D-glucan, an essential structural component of the cell wall of many filamentous fungi and yeasts. Disruption of glucan synthesis compromises cell-wall integrity and produces fungicidal or fungistatic effects depending on the organism.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (e.g. anaphylaxis) to caspofungin or any component of the product
relative: Concomitant cyclosporine (limit to patients where benefit outweighs risk; monitor LFTs)
Pre-existing hepatic dysfunction or abnormal liver enzymes
monitor: Liver function tests, especially with cyclosporine co-administration
Signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity during infusion

preg: Based on animal data, caspofungin may cause fetal harm. In rats and rabbits it caused embryofetal toxicity (increased resorptions, peri-implantation loss, incomplete ossification, cervical rib) at exposures up to 0.8 and 2 times the clinical dose, and it crossed the placenta. Human data are insufficient to establish a drug-associated risk. Advise patients of the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether caspofungin is present in human milk, or its effects on the breastfed infant or on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary based on renal function. Caspofungin is not dialyzable, so no supplemental dosing is needed after hemodialysis.
hepatic: For adult patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score 7-9), reduce the daily maintenance dose to 35 mg once daily (a 70 mg loading dose on Day 1 is still recommended where appropriate). No data are available in adults with severe hepatic impairment or in pediatric patients with any degree of hepatic impairment.

major: Rifampin (potent CYP3A4 inducer) - reduces caspofungin levels; use 70 mg daily in adults
moderate: Cyclosporine - increases caspofungin AUC with transient ALT/AST rises; limit use and monitor LFTs
Other hepatic CYP inducers (efavirenz, nevirapine, phenytoin, dexamethasone, carbamazepine) - consider 70 mg daily in adults
Tacrolimus - monitor tacrolimus trough levels and adjust its dose
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor liver function tests during therapy, particularly with concomitant cyclosporine

serious: Clinically significant hepatic dysfunction, hepatitis, or hepatic failure
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), some fatal
emergency: Anaphylaxis or histamine-mediated reaction during infusion (rash, facial swelling, angioedema, bronchospasm)

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase), especially with cyclosporine
Signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity during and after infusion
counsel: This antifungal is given as a slow IV infusion, usually over about 1 hour
Report rash, itching, facial or throat swelling, or trouble breathing during the infusion
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or abdominal pain (possible liver effects)
Tell your team if you take cyclosporine, tacrolimus, rifampin, or anti-seizure medicines
pk: Plasma levels achieved during the 1-hour IV infusion
End of the 1-hour infusion; extensively albumin bound (~97%)
Beta-phase half-life 9-11 hours; longer gamma-phase 40-50 hours
Once-daily dosing; distribution rather than excretion governs clearance
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C (36-46 F); discard unused portion
pearls: Reduce maintenance dose to 35 mg daily in moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh 7-9); no data in severe impairment
No renal dose adjustment and not dialyzable
Increase to 70 mg daily with rifampin (and consider with other CYP inducers)
Esophageal candidiasis uses 50 mg daily with no loading dose
Do not use dextrose-containing diluents; infuse over 1 hour, never as a bolus
Pediatric dosing is by body surface area (70 mg/m2 load, 50 mg/m2 daily), capped at 70 mg
missed: Not applicable for patient self-administration - caspofungin is given by a clinician as a once-daily IV infusion; a missed or delayed dose should be administered as soon as feasible per the treating team without doubling up.
overdose: In healthy subjects a single 210 mg dose produced no significant adverse reactions, and doses above 150 mg daily have not been studied; one 16-year-old who received 113 mg then 80 mg daily for 7 days had no clinically significant reactions. Caspofungin is not dialyzable. Manage overdose with supportive care and monitoring.
